Rashi on Menachot 96a:10:1.hebrew: וטפחיים ריוח באמצע - בין שתי הסדרים. דרוחב הלחם אינו אלא ה', ושני הסדרים מחזיקים י' טפחים, כאורך השלחן פשו להו טפחיים, והם ריוח בין סדר לסדר, שתהא רוח מנשבת בהם שלא יתעפשו:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:10:1.english: And two handbreadths of space in the middle - Between the two arrangements. For the width of the bread is only five [handbreadths], and the two arrangements occupy ten handbreadths; [so] along the length of the Table, two handbreadths remained, and they are the space between one arrangement and the other, so that air may blow through them, so that they do not become moldy.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:11:1.hebrew: אבא שאול אומר שם - באותו ריוח שבין סדר לסדר, בו נותנין בזיכים:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:11:1.english: Abba Shaul says: There - In that space between [one] stack and [the other] stack, in it they would place the bowls [of frankincense].

Rashi on Menachot 96a:11:3.english: And next to him the tribe - That [instance of] “al” means adjacent.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:12:1.hebrew: המפוצלים - לתת ראשי הקנים באותן פיצולין, והרבה פיצולין יש בהן למנין הקנים:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:12:1.english: Forked - To place the ends of the rods into those forks, and there were many forks in them, corresponding to the number of rods.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:12:2.english: Twenty-eight rods - In the Gemara it explains how many rods [were placed] for [each] loaf.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:13:1.hebrew: לא סידור הקנים - במערכת החדשה, ולא נטילתן מעל הישנה, דוחה שבת:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:13:1.english: Neither the arranging of the rods - In the new arrangement, nor their removal from upon the old [arrangement], overrides Shabbat.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:13:2.hebrew: שומטן - מבין כל לחם ולחם, ומניחן לאורכו של שלחן. ולמחר מסדר הלחם, ולמוצאי שבת נותן הקנים בין כל לחם ולחם כמשפטן:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:13:2.english: He pulls them out - From between each and every loaf, and places them along the length of the Table. And on the morrow, he arranges the bread, and at the conclusion of Shabbat, he places the rods between each and every loaf in their proper manner.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:14:1.hebrew: כל הכלים - כגון שולחנות, אורכן לאורכו של בית, ממזרח למערב:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:14:1.english: All the vessels - Such as the tables: their length was along the length of the House, from east to west.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:15:1.english: From where is this - That the meal offerings require a vessel.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:16:1.hebrew: מה חטאת ואשם טעונין כלי - דכתיב אשר יבשלו, ואין בישול בלא כלי. ובפנים משתעי קרא, דכתיב (יחזקאל מ״ו:כ׳) לבלתי הוציא אל החיצונות:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:16:1.english: Just as a sin-offering and a guilt-offering require a vessel - For it is written: "where they shall boil," and there is no boiling without a vessel. And the verse is speaking of [cooking] inside [the courtyard], as it is written (Ezekiel 46:20): "so as not to bring [them] out to the outer [court]."

Rashi on Menachot 96a:18:1.hebrew: ט"ו טפחים - ב' טפחים ומחצה לכל לחם, והם שש חלות זו על גב זו, נמצא שלחן מקדש כו'. ונפקא מינה, דאי יהיב באויר השלחן מידי בתוך ט"ו טפחים, מקדש ליה ליפסל בלינה:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:18:1.english: Fifteen handbreadths - Two and a half handbreadths for each loaf, and they are six loaves one on top of the other; [thus] it emerges that the Table consecrates, etc. And the practical difference is that if one places anything in the airspace of the Table within fifteen handbreadths, [the Table] consecrates it, so that it becomes disqualified by remaining overnight.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:19:1.hebrew: והאיכא קנים - שבין כל לחם ולחם, ואיכא טפי:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:19:1.english: And aren't there canes - That are between each and every loaf, and [so] there is more [height]?

Rashi on Menachot 96a:19:2.hebrew: משקע להו - פגימות עושה בלחם בעוד שהיה בצק, והקנים היו משוקעים בהם, ואינו מגביה הלחם:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:19:2.english: He would embed them - He would make indentations in the bread while it was still dough, and the canes were embedded in them, and [this] did not raise the bread.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:1:1.hebrew: מסוכן הוא - שאחזו בולמוס. ותנן: מי שאחזו בולמוס מאכילין אותו עד שיאורו עיניו, אפילו ביום הכפורים, ביומא בפרק בתרא (דף פג.):
Rashi on Menachot 96a:1:1.english: He is dangerously ill - That ravenous hunger had seized him. And we learned in a mishna: One who was seized by ravenous hunger is fed until his eyes light up, even on Yom Kippur, in [tractate] Yoma, in the final chapter (83a).

Rashi on Menachot 96a:1:2.hebrew: בגמ' פליגי - מר גמיר ליה מרביה דתנור מקדש, ומר גמיר דלא מקדש:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:1:2.english: They disagree over a tradition - One learned from his teacher that the oven sanctifies, and one learned that it does not sanctify.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:20:1.hebrew: וקא פריך מאי טעמא - כלומר, מכדי קנים מאי טעמא היו בין כל לחם:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:20:1.english: And [the Gemara] asks: What is the reason - That is to say: After all, what was the reason that there were rods between each loaf?

Rashi on Menachot 96a:20:2.hebrew: משום איעפושי - שיהא אויר בינתים, שלא יתעפשו:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:20:2.english: Because of moldiness - That there should be air in between, so that they will not become moldy.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:20:3.hebrew: סוף סוף - כיון דמשקע להו, ליכא אוירא ומיעפש הלחם:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:20:3.english: Ultimately - Since he embeds them [in the bread], there is no air, and the bread will become moldy.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:20:4.english: Slightly - So that it would not be sunken so much.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:22:1.hebrew: והאיכא בזיכין - קשיא לי: אמאי פריך הכי? דהא שלחן לא מקדש להו לבזיכין:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:22:1.english: And are there not the bowls? - It is difficult to me: Why does [the Gemara] ask this? For the Table does not sanctify the bowls.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:22:2.english: But aren't there horns - Which protrude and are fashioned at the top of the wall [of the loaf].

Rashi on Menachot 96a:2:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי - דבגמרא פליגי ולא בקראי, מדנקט האי לישנא: לעולם הוי רגיל לומר כו':
Rashi on Menachot 96a:2:1.english: [The wording is] also precise - That they disagree over an oral tradition and not over verses, since he used this phrasing: "One should always be accustomed to saying, etc."

Rashi on Menachot 96a:3:1.hebrew: חביתי כהן גדול לישתן ועריכתן בפנים - ולדברי הכל, אותו חצי עשרון שהיה חולק בו עשרונו של כהן גדול נמשח. והאי דלא משחו עשרון שלם - מפני שכל אדם מודד בו מנחתו, דפעמים שמוציאו לחוץ, אבל זה אינו מסור אלא לכהנים, לחצות בו עשרונים:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:3:1.english: The High Priest’s griddle cakes: Their kneading and their shaping are inside - And according to all opinions, that half-tenth [measure] with which one would divide the High Priest’s tenth [of an ephah] was anointed [as a service vessel]. And the reason that they did not anoint a full tenth [measure] is because any person measures his meal offering with it, as at times he takes it outside [the Temple courtyard]; but this [measure] was entrusted only to priests, to divide tenths with it.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:3:2.hebrew: ושא"א - אפייתן אי אפשר לעשות מאתמול, ולא לישה ועריכה, דכיון דקדשה בכלי מיפסל בלינה:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:3:2.english: And that which is impossible - Their baking cannot be done yesterday [on Friday], nor [can] kneading and shaping, for since it was sanctified in a [service] vessel, it becomes disqualified by remaining overnight.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:4:1.hebrew: מעשה כלי - לישה ועריכה, הכל בכלי שרת, בפנים ולא בחוץ:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:4:1.english: Action with a vessel - Kneading and shaping: all [are done] in a service vessel, inside [the Courtyard] and not outside.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:5:1.hebrew: וקרנותיה - שהיה מדביק בצק לכל זוית כעין קרנים, ואורך הקרן ד' אצבעות:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:5:1.english: And its horns - That he would attach dough to each corner like horns, and the length of the horn was four fingerbreadths.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:6:1.hebrew: שלא תטעה - בין שתי הלחם ללחם הפנים, בין בשיעור רוחב, בין בשיעור אורך וקרנות:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:6:1.english: That you will not err - Between the two loaves and the showbread, whether in the measure of width, or in the measure of length and the horns.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:6:2.hebrew: זד"ד יה"ז - זד"ד: שתי הלחם – אורכה ז', ורחבה ד', וקרנותיה ד'. יה"ז: לחם הפנים – ארכו י', ורחבו ה', וקרנותיו ז':
Rashi on Menachot 96a:6:2.english: Zedad Yehaz - Zedad: The Two Loaves — its length was seven [handbreadths], its width was four [handbreadths], and its horns were four [fingerbreadths]. Yehaz: The Showbread — its length was ten [handbreadths], its width was five [handbreadths], and its horns were seven [fingerbreadths].

Rashi on Menachot 96a:6:3.hebrew: שיהא לו פנים - דפנות. [ל"א]: שיהא לו פנים - זויות, והן הן הקרנות:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:6:3.english: That it should have faces - [Vertical] sides. [Another explanation: “That it should have faces” - Corners, and these are the horns.]

Rashi on Menachot 96a:7:1.hebrew: ארכו י' ורחבו ה' - כדכתיב: אמתים ארכו ואמה רחבו, ור' יהודה לטעמיה, דאמר: אמת כלים באמת בת ה'. ונותן אורכו של לחם כנגד רוחבו של שלחן:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:7:1.english: Its length was ten and its width five - As it is written: “Two cubits its length, and a cubit its width” [Exodus 25:23], and Rabbi Yehuda follows his [standard] reasoning, as he said that the cubit of the vessels was a cubit of five [handbreadths]. And he places the length of the bread across the width of the Table.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:8:2.hebrew: טפחיים ומחצה - למעלה מיכן ומיכן, ובהן הן הקרנות, ונמצאו זקופות בשוה לשפת השלחן. ולמ"ד כמין ספינה רוקדת, הוו הנך דפנות הולכות וזוקפות בשיפוע:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:8:2.english: Two and a half handbreadths - [Folded] upward on this side and on that side, and on them are the horns; and thus they stand upright, flush with the edge of the Table. And according to the one who says [it was shaped] like a rocking boat, these walls would rise upward at an incline.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:8:3.hebrew: ונמצא ארכו ממלא רחבו של שלחן - ורחבן מחזיק חצי אורך השלחן, וכשהיה סודר האחר אצלו, נמצא שלחן כולו מלא:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:8:3.english: And its length turns out to fill the width of the Table - And their width takes up half the length of the Table, and when he would arrange the other [stack] next to it, the entire Table turned out to be filled.

Rashi on Menachot 96a:9:1.hebrew: אורכו י"ב - ר' מאיר לטעמיה, דאמר: כל האמות היו בבינונית. והלחם עשרה, דבהא לא פליג:
Rashi on Menachot 96a:9:1.english: Its length was twelve - Rabbi Meir [follows] his reasoning, as he said: All the cubits were of standard [measure]. And the bread was ten [handbreadths], for regarding this he does not disagree.

Tosafot on Menachot 96a:14:1.hebrew: כל הכלים שהיו במקדש אורכן לאורכו של בית - בגמ' תניא: חוץ מארון שאורכו לרוחבו של בית. ובשולחן ומנורה פליגי רבי ור' אלעזר בר' שמעון, ומתני' כרבי, דאמר: מזרח ומערב מונחין:
Tosafot on Menachot 96a:14:1.english: All the vessels that were in the Temple, their length was along the length of the House - In the Gemara it is taught: Except for the Ark, whose length was along the width of the House. And regarding the Table and the Menorah, Rabbi and Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon disagree, and our Mishnah is in accordance with Rabbi, who said [they were] placed east to west.

Tosafot on Menachot 96a:15:1.hebrew: שאלו את רבי זו מנין - אמתני' קאי וקאמר: מנין שכל המנחות יש בהן מעשה כלי בפנים? ולא לענין קמיצה מכלי שרת וקידוש קומץ בכלי שרת איירי, דבהאי קרא דמייתי איירי בבישול חטאת ואשם ואפיית מנחה, ולא מיירי בקידוש קומץ כלל. ומהיקשא ד"זאת התורה" נפקא לן לעיל בסוף פ' התודה (מנחות דף פב:): מה עולה טעונה כלי, דכתיב: "ויקח את המאכלת", אף כל טעון כלי; וקמיצה כנגד שחיטה, וקידוש קומץ כנגד קבלה, כדאמר לעיל בפ' שני (מנחות דף יג:). אלא הכא בלישה ועריכה ואפיה של מנחה מיירי, דאיתקש אפיה דמנחה לבישול דחטאת ואשם: מה הם טעונין כלי — דכתיב: "וכלי חרס אשר תבושל בו ישבר ואם בכלי נחושת בושלה", ומיהו מזה אין ראיה, דלאו למירמי חובה קאמר, אלא כדפירש בקונטרס, דכתיב: "אשר תבושל בו", ואין בישול בלא כלי; ובפנים משתעי קרא, דאי בחוץ, הרי חטאת ואשם נפסל ביוצא, ועוד כתיב ביה: "לבלתי הוציא אל [החצר] החיצונה" — אף אפיה דמנחה טעונין כלי שרת, והוא הדין לישה ועריכה. וצריך לדקדק: לאיזו מנחה איצטריך קרא? אי למנחת מחבת ומרחשת ומאפה תנור — הא כתיב בהו כלי! ואילו למנחת סלת — אין בה אפיה קודם קמיצה:
Tosafot on Menachot 96a:15:1.english: They asked Rabbi: From where is this derived? - [The Gemara's question] relates to the Mishnah, asking: From where is it derived that all meal-offerings involve the use of a vessel inside [the Temple courtyard]? And it is not dealing with removing the fistful (kemitzah) from a service vessel or sanctifying the fistful in a service vessel, for in this verse that [Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi] cites, it speaks of cooking the sin-offering and guilt-offering and baking the meal-offering, and does not speak of the sanctification of the fistful at all. Furthermore, [the requirement of a vessel for the fistful] is derived for us above at the end of the chapter "Ha-Todah" (Menachot 82b) from the juxtaposition in the verse "This is the law [of the burnt-offering, of the meal-offering...]" (Leviticus 7:37): just as a burnt-offering requires a vessel, as it is written: "And [Abraham] took the knife" (Genesis 22:10), so too everything requires a vessel; and kemitzah corresponds to slaughter, while sanctifying the fistful corresponds to receiving [the blood], as stated above in the second chapter (Menachot 13b). Rather, here it is dealing with the kneading, shaping, and baking of a meal-offering, for the baking of a meal-offering is juxtaposed to the cooking of a sin-offering and a guilt-offering: just as they require a vessel — [if one suggests this is] because it is written, "And the earthen vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken, and if it was cooked in a copper vessel..." (Leviticus 6:21), yet from this there is no proof, for it did not come to impose an obligation [to cook in a vessel], but rather as Rashi explained, for it is written "in which it is cooked," and there is no cooking without a vessel; and the verse speaks of [cooking] inside [the courtyard], for if [cooked] outside, a sin-offering and guilt-offering would be disqualified by having left [the sacred precincts], and furthermore it is written concerning it: "that they do not bring them out to the outer courtyard" (Ezekiel 46:20) — so too, the baking of a meal-offering requires a service vessel, and the same applies to its kneading and shaping. And it requires careful analysis: for which meal-offering was this verse necessary? If for a pan (maḥavat), deep pan (marḥeshet), or oven-baked (ma'afeh tanur) meal-offering — a vessel is already written explicitly concerning them! While for a fine-flour meal-offering (minḥat solet) — there is no baking before the fistful is removed.

Tosafot on Menachot 96a:22:1.hebrew: והאיכא בזיכין - הקשה בקונטרס: אמאי פריך הכי, דהא שולחן לא מקדש להו לבזיכין? ונראה דלא קשה (ליה) מידי, דהא אמרינן בפ"ק (לעיל מנחות דף ז.) דקומץ מנחה מכלי שעל גבי קרקע, שכן מצינו בסילוק בזיכין, משמע דהוי כקומץ מע"ג השלחן:
Tosafot on Menachot 96a:22:1.english: But aren't there the bowls - Rashi asked in his commentary: Why does [the Gemara] ask this, given that the Table does not sanctify the bowls? And it seems that this is not difficult at all, for we say in the first chapter (above, 7a) that one may remove a handful of a meal-offering from a vessel that is resting on the ground, as we find with the removal of the bowls [of frankincense] — which implies that it is considered like removing a handful from upon the Table.

Tosafot on Menachot 96a:3:1.hebrew: כלל א"ר עקיבא כו' - בפ' ר"א אומר אם לא הביא (שבת דף קלג. ושם) ובפ' אלו דברים (פסחים דף סט:) פסק כר' עקיבא, משום דאיכא צריכותא גבי פסח ומילה; אבל הכא, ליכא צריכותא. ומיהו, אמילתיה דר"ע לא בעי צריכותא, דאשמעינן בכל דוכתא מאי דדחי שבת:
Tosafot on Menachot 96a:3:1.english: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle, etc. - In the chapter "Rabbi Eliezer Says: If He Did Not Bring" (Shabbat 133a and there) and in the chapter "These Matters" (Pesachim 69b), [Rav] ruled in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, because there is a need [to state both cases] regarding the Paschal offering and circumcision; but here, there is no [such] need. However, regarding Rabbi Akiva's own statement, no [such] need is required, for he is teaching us in each place what overrides Shabbat.
